correctness.rationale: Scoville supplies integral homotopy classification of exactly the non-pure boundary complex, giving rational H3,H4 ranks 21 and 24 and exact rational boundary ranks d5=256,d4=968,d3=703. The packaged standard-library program exhaustively constructs all 4332 nonempty acyclic Hasse matching simplices, computes orientation-signed fixed chain sums under every ten S4×C2 conjugacy types and powers, and verifies all invariant differentials over distinct primes 1009 and 10007. Their group element orders are coprime to both primes; averaging yields a direct-sum splitting over localized integers, and since whole-differential modular ranks equal published rational ranks, each invariant-summand rank is exact in characteristic zero. Cyclotomic inversion gives actual separate H3/H4 traces, independently checked by ten signed simplicial Lefschetz sums; all twenty irreducible multiplicities satisfy exact character orthogonality and nonnegative integer tests. Limitations: finite implementation and explicit dependence on published nonequivariant homotopy theorem; not a fresh proof of that source theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Scoville supplies the non-equivariant sphere counts and the group-theoretic study supplies automorphisms. The full tetrahedron ordinary Morse character has only 99-dimensional degree-four homology. The generalized matching complex explicitly drops acyclicity and has a 39-dimensional fourth-homology representation. Neither a different complex’s character nor the original homotopy types imply the two graded boundary characters or ghost splitting.

value.rationale: The natural non-pure tetrahedral boundary Morse complex is the smallest established example with adjacent homology degrees 3 and 4, and its full S4×ghost automorphism group is canonical. Separately resolving 21- and 24-dimensional graded modules, opposite ghost-parity splits, and distinctions between geometric full and rotational quotients supplies structural representation and quotient information not implied by the known sphere counts or relative virtual character. The precise finite invariant is motivated by the already known group action and mixed-dimensional topology, and it determines all subgroup rational quotient homology by character restriction.
